Port and Water Transport Terminal Operations

merger_description:
Sinopec (Hong Kong) Limited (**Sinopec**) proposes to acquire (directly or via a wholly owned subsidiary) 75% of the issued and outstanding shares of Bintan Pty Limited and Australian Terminals Pty Limited and their respective subsidiaries (which are collectively the holding companies of the **Park Fuels** business) (the **Acquisition**).

Sinopec is a subsidiary of the China Petrochemical Corporation (**Sinopec Group**), a Chinese, state-owned oil and gas enterprise. Sinopec Group's activities include oil and gas exploration and production, oil refining, petrochemicals and chemical products, and the import and export of crude oil, natural gas, refining oil products, and chemicals. In Australia, Sinopec Group (through its subsidiaries) is engaged in the wholesale and retail supply of fuel products in Victoria and Western Australia, as well as the supply of coal, petrochemical products, and equipment and materials produced by Sinopec Group.

Park Fuels is an Australian fuel supply company headquartered in Albion Park Rail, New South Wales. Park Fuels imports fuel into Australia via its terminal operations at Kooragang Island and Port Kembla in New South Wales, and offers fuel terminal and storage services to third parties from these locations. Park Fuels is also engaged in the wholesale supply of fuel, primarily in New South Wales and Queensland, and operates fuel retail sites in various locations across New South Wales.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
Based on the information provided in the application, including the
parties’ (and their connected entities) revenues in Australia, the
ACCC considers it is likely that, if the Acquisition were put into effect,
the notification thresholds would be met.
The ACCC is unable to reach a view that the Acquisition would not be
likely to raise competition issues in any market based on the
information provided, given:
a. there are multiple potential vertical relationships
between the products and services supplied by the
parties in Australia, and the impact of the Acquisition on
the merged entity’s ability and/or incentive to foreclose
rivals is uncertain
b. the extent to which the merged entity would likely be
constrained by alternative providers of fuel terminal and
storage services in New South Wales or elsewhere in
Australia is unclear
c. it is unclear whether Sinopec Group would otherwise
expand its operations in Australia absent the Acquisition
and therefore, whether the Acquisition may result in a
loss of future competition.
The ACCC considers that the Acquisition warrants consideration
through the notification process, including via consultation with third
parties.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
